extracted.intended_audience: LEAs, IHEs, State and national athletic associations, athletic directors, attorneys, and other Title IX stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register preamble and regulatory impact analysis proposing a Title IX regulatory standard for sex-related eligibility criteria for participation on male and female athletic teams, including assumptions and cost estimates for LEAs, IHEs, and athletic associations. Useful for stakeholders preparing comments on the proposed rule and its economic/legal analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients' obligation to comply with Title IX regardless of athletic association rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient LEAs and IHEs must comply with Title IX and the obligation to do so is not alleviated by any contrary athletic association rule (see 34 CFR 106.6(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes that athletic-association-imposed requirements do not relieve recipients of their Title IX obligations; recipients should review association policies for compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed regulatory standard (Option 4) for sex-related eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposes a regulatory standard that can be effectively implemented, consistent with Title IX, by recipients serving students at varying grade and education levels in a variety of male and female team sports at varying levels of competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department's view is that this standard would clarify legal obligations, better ensure nondiscrimination, and strike an appropriate balance given unique athletic considerations; it should allow assessment of grade/education level, nature of sport, and level of competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of alternatives (1–3) and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department considered: (1) leaving current regulations unchanged; (2) addressing issue through guidance; (3) proposing amendments to specify permissible eligibility requirements—but rejected these in favor of (4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: (1) leaving unchanged is unreasonable given developments; (2) guidance is not legally binding and won't establish recipients' legal obligations; (3) specifying permissible requirements would not allow assessment tailored to grade level, sport nature, competition level, or other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that all regulated entities complete an initial review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assumes all regulated entities, including those that do not offer athletic programs, will take time to review the proposed regulation to determine whether it applies to their entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated as a baseline compliance activity and is the basis for initial cost estimates (see task-specific time/cost assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption about prevalence of LEAs offering sex-separate teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 60 percent of LEAs are assumed to offer one or more male or female athletic teams, leading to an estimated 10,849 affected LEAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption is based on 2017–2018 Civil Rights Data Collection and underpins estimates of affected entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State athletic associations' expected policy-review and revision split
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of analysis, Department assumes: (a) all LEAs will engage in an initial review; (b) in 20% of States, associations and LEAs with policies already permitting participation will review but unlikely revise; (c) in 20% of States, associations with permissive requirements enabling participation will undertake more intensive review but unlikely revise; (d) in 60% of States, associations and LEAs with prohibitive or restrictive policies will undertake intensive review and will revise existing policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department seeks public comment on these percentage assumptions and on whether categories should be subdivided to reflect variation in procedural/bureaucratic structures across associations and States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption of equal distribution of LEAs across States for impact estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: Because LEAs are not evenly distributed, the Department nonetheless assumes that if X% of State athletic associations implement a policy, X% of LEAs offering athletic teams would be affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department notes this is a simplifying assumption due to lack of state-level granular data and requests comments and data to improve state-specific estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption on timing and frequency of State athletic association reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department assumes an initial review prompted by the proposed regulation, followed in later years by approximately five State athletic associations reviewing these policies each year, of which about one will revise its policy each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department considers periodic reviews likely but anticipates they will generally be several years after the initial review; requests comment on the reasonableness of the timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption that additional training burdens will be minimal for LEAs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department anticipates relatively low numbers of transgender student-athletes and assumes any additional training required beyond standard athletic-director training will be ad hoc and will not create additional time burdens above baseline in future years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes new training will largely supplant other training or be absorbed into existing training schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE entities: baseline review and percentages for intensive review and revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: All IHEs (including those that do not offer teams) will complete an initial review; 40% of IHEs (those offering athletic teams) will undertake a more intensive review; 20% of IHEs will revise institution-specific policies; all five named athletic associations and two additional associations will extensively review their policies, and of those seven associations, four will revise policies; as a result of association changes, 10% of IHEs will conduct a secondary review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department expects larger, better-resourced IHEs to conduct independent reviews of revised association policies; requests comment on these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumption on national athletic associations' periodic review/revision cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Department assumes national athletic associations will periodically review and update policies, are unlikely to review them for several years after initial review, but thereafter approximately two national athletic associations will review these policies each year and most associations review on a ~3-year cycle; approximately one association will revise policies each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department seeks comment on whether this timeline and rate of revision are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA initial review time/cost assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: At the LEA level, the initial review is estimated to take approximately half an hour for an education administrator at $100.36/hour across 18,083 LEAs, resulting in a Year 1 cost estimate of $907,400.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used to monetize baseline compliance burden; Department welcomes comments on time and wage assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA and State athletic association less intensive review time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For less intensive reviews (20% of States): LEAs—2 hours each from an education administrator and a management analyst ($81.56/hour) at 2,169 LEAs; State athletic associations—4 hours EA, 4 hours MA, 2 hours attorney ($148.76/hour) at each of 10 associations; total estimated Year 1 cost ≈ $799,420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department requests comments on these hour and wage assumptions and the number of associations/states in this category.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEA and State athletic association more intensive review time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For more intensive reviews (80% of States): LEAs—4 hours each for an education administrator and a management analyst in 8,679 LEAs; State associations—6 hours EA, 6 hours MA, and 2 hours attorney for each of 41 associations; total estimated Year 1 cost ≈ $6,372,490.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions drive larger-cost estimates; Department seeks comment and evidence on review times and staffing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: State athletic association policy revision time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes 60% of State athletic associations will revise policies: LEA involvement—one education administrator spending 4 hours at each of 6,509 LEAs; State association work—4 hours EA, 20 hours MA, and 12 hours attorney for each of 31 associations; total Year 1 estimated cost ≈ $2,731,320.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department assumes revising will take less time than review because issues were identified during review; requests comment on these estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: State athletic association training development and delivery time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: After revisions, development: 10 hours MA, 10 hours lawyer, and 1 hour EA to review/approve training in each of 31 associations. Delivery: additional 30 minutes above existing training for an education administrator at each of 6,509 LEAs. Total Year 1 estimated cost ≈ $401,130.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes associations already provide training annually and new content would be integrated into existing training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-year recurrent review/revision cost assumptions for State associations
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginning in Year 3, the Department assumes ≈5 State athletic associations per year undertake a review (1 hour EA, 4 hours MA, 2 hours lawyer) costing ≈$3,620 per year; one of those will opt to revise policies (4 hours EA, 16 hours MA, 10 hours lawyer) costing ≈$3,190 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These figures are used to estimate ongoing annualized costs after initial implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present value monetized cost estimate for ESE entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department estimates the proposed regulation would generate a present value monetized cost of $10.5 to $10.9 million over 10 years, assuming a seven percent and three percent discount rate, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This PV estimate aggregates the ESE (elementary/secondary education) assumptions and cost items described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE initial review time/cost assumption
rubrics_metrics.description: IHEs: initial review estimated at approximately 1 hour by an education administrator at each of 6,045 IHEs for a total Year 1 cost of $607,580.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the IHE baseline compliance activity; Department requests comment on time and wage assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE internal policy review time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: For IHEs offering athletic teams, internal policy review estimated at 8 hours EA, 8 hours MA, and 6 hours attorney per each of 2,148 IHEs, totaling ≈$5,043,330 in Year 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes legal and administrative resources are used at larger IHEs; Department seeks comment on these assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IHE policy revision time/cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Approximately 20% of IHEs (1,210 IHEs) expected to revise institution-specific policies requiring 4 hours EA, 30 hours MA, and 16 hours attorney per IHE, totaling ≈$6,326,360 in Year 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions feed into the aggregate IHE cost estimates; Department requests data on typical revision workloads.

rubrics_metrics.name: National athletic associations' review and revision time/cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Department assumes all five named associations plus two additional associations (7 total) will review their policies requiring 8 hours each from four education administrators, 8 hours each from four management analysts, and 6 hours each from two attorneys, totaling ≈$53,250 in Year 1. It further assumes four of those associations will revise policies (15 hours EA, 20 hours MA, 12 hours attorney) and that ~10% of IHEs will do a secondary review; total revision-related costs ≈$1,484,960. Training updates by those associations estimated ≈$148,970 in Year 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department acknowledges association sizes vary and policy changes by one association (e.g., NCAA) could have disproportionate effects; requests comment on association-level effects and alignment incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future-year national association review/revision cost assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Department assumes approximately two national athletic associations per year would undertake a review (cost ≈$12,000/year beginning Year 3) and that one of those would opt to revise its policies each year (cost ≈$11,410/year beginning Year 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to estimate ongoing national-association administrative costs; Department seeks comment on plausibility of these rates and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present value monetized cost estimate for IHE entities
rubrics_metrics.description: At the IHE level, the Department estimates total present value monetized costs of $12.9 to $13.4 million over 10 years, assuming seven percent and three percent discount rates, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aggregates the IHE-level baseline, review, revision, training, and association-related costs described above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting statement categories and annualized cost table
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are categorized and annualized (3% and 7% discount rates) across categories: Preliminary Review of the Regulation; Review of Policies; Revision of Policies; Updated Training; Periodic Review of Policies; Periodic Updating of Policies. The table shows annualized dollar amounts and notes benefits (clarity; protecting equal opportunity and health) are not quantified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department invites comments on whether these categories, amounts, and the non-quantified benefits appropriately capture regulatory impacts and on ways to improve clarity and quantification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-language clarity questions for commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 12866 and the Presidential memorandum on plain language require clear regulations; the Secretary invites comments addressing: Are requirements clearly stated? Do technical terms interfere with clarity? Does format (headings, paragraphing) aid clarity? Would dividing into more/shorter sections help? Would the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION description be more helpful? What else could make the regulation easier to understand?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To send comments on clarity, follow ADDRESSES instructions in the preamble. The Department seeks specific suggestions for wording, structure, and explanatory material.
